Definition: from the same as G3116; to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient:--bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure.
BiblicalUsage: Makrothumeo means to be long-spirited, to bear long, to be patient, and it is both God's character and the believer's command. 1 Corinthians 13:4 says charity suffereth long, and is kind, and 2 Peter 3:9 says the Lord is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish. James 5:7 tells the brethren, be patient unto the coming of the Lord, as the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is the patience of God made visible: He bears long with us, and then He asks us to bear long with each other. My position is that 2 Peter 3:9 is the reason for all of it, because His longsuffering is not slowness but mercy, waiting for sinners to come home.
